The port's physics · car census · measurements

Car census: every car, classic and modern

The port can drive GT2 on two kinds of physics: classic, GT2's own, exactly as on the PlayStation, and modern, the port's optional physics based on real-world formulas. Here every car of the GT mode database (618) was run on both, with the same automated drivers on the same courses. The question: does modern physics move every car by about the same amount, by group, or one car at a time? Nothing here changes the physics or the car data; it only measures.

618cars measured (0 excluded)
-0.7 %median 0-100 km/h change (uniform, 11 outliers)
-1.0 %median lap time change (shifts by power-to-weight)
+0.4 %median skidpad grip change (scattered, car by car)
-1.1 %median braking 100-0 change (uniform, 36 outliers)

Verdict

Mostly uniform. Modern physics makes almost every car about 1 % quicker in a straight line and on a lap, keeps the order of the cars nearly the same, and moves cornering grip car by car.

  • Classic is GT2. The classic numbers are the original game's behavior; every difference on this page is modern's.
  • One- and two-gear cars. Modern has GT2's hybrid 1-speed box and its 2-speed CVT. The Toyota Prius reaches 100 km/h in 13.23 s and tops out at 186 km/h on both. The Honda Logo tops out at 181 km/h (classic 178), reaches 100 km/h in 13.8 s and laps Autumn Ring in 99.0 s (classic 100.2).
  • 4WD cars with a stiff center coupling. HKS Drag R33: 0-200 km/h 6.73 s on modern against 8.27 s on classic. The GT500 R33s reach about 350 km/h on modern; their roughly 6 % lower top speed than classic comes from classic's own power surplus near 345 km/h.
  • The fully tuned GT-Rs (yaw-dependent 4WD) launch within about 2 % of classic; only the R33 4-Door stays about 6 % slower to 100 km/h.
  • The HKS lap outlier. The HKS Drag R33 is the biggest lap rank move (rank 608 to 105, 86.2 s against classic's 107.3). That is the AI hitting the walls 18 times on classic, not physics. Lap times of the AWD codes 4 and 5 are sensitive: one changed physics step can move a lap by tenths.
  • Still being looked at: heavy front-engine cars that stop much shorter on modern (modern is the real-physics side here), the road R33 GT-Rs' top speed, and the GT90 and Corvette launches.

Change = (modern - classic) / classic, in percent. Positive = modern takes longer / stops longer / goes faster / grips more, by metric. Drivetrain span = the largest gap between the medians of groups with 5+ cars. eta2 = the share of the change that the drivetrain grouping explains (0 = none, 1 = all; extreme cars clipped). p10 .. p90 = the range that holds the middle 80 % of cars.

Changes by drivetrain

Each row is one drivetrain group (4WD split by GT2's drive code: 2 front-primary viscous, 3 rigid center, 4 fixed split, 5 yaw-dependent split, 6 open center). The box is the middle half of the cars, the line through it the middle 80 %, the dark tick the median, each dot one car (hover for its name). The vertical line is no change; the axis spans the 1st to 99th percentile, so the few cars past it sit on the edge.

Classic against modern

Every car once: classic on the x axis, modern on the y axis. On the diagonal = no change; a uniform shift moves the cloud off the diagonal as a band; a car off the band is an outlier (highlighted and labeled: the largest differences from their drivetrain group).

Outliers

Compared with the car's drivetrain group median: more than the metric's threshold in percentage points (5 for 0-100, 0-200, braking and the skidpad; 3 for 400 m and top speed; 2 for the lap), or more than 2 standard deviations and at least half the threshold. The short codes are the cars' IDs in the game's database.

Rank order

Does modern physics reshuffle which car is faster? Spearman rho measures how well two rankings agree: 1 means the same order, 0 means unrelated.

A swapped pair = two cars whose order flips between classic and modern. A flip between cars that were within 2 % of each other on classic is close to noise; a flip across a clear gap is a real change in the order.

How it was measured

  • Straight: full throttle from the race start on an endless flat straight (a wall-free tarmac plane; the car is moved back 900 m each time it nears the edge), the wheel held straight; 0-100, 0-200 km/h and 400 m from the body speed, the top speed where the speed gains under 0.5 km/h in 10 s.
  • Braking: on the same straight, full throttle to 120 km/h, then full brake; distance and time from 100 km/h to rest.
  • Skidpad: a 50 m and a 60 m circle on the plane; steady runs (a steering controller holds the circle, a speed controller the speed, 7 s at each speed); the highest speed held before the first loss of grip (a rising scan, then narrowing down) and its sideways g; the page shows the mean of the two radii.
  • Lap: a Free Run of Autumn Ring with GT2's own AI driving on both physics, two laps; the second (flying) lap counts.
  • Cross-check: the top-speed Machine Test with GT2's AI driving one lap (the AI does not get 60 low-power cars going there).
  • Every car with its stock spec (the garage set-up of a new car).
